rationale: The Court is most likely to uphold SB1 in a Roberts opinion that treats it as an age- and indication-based medical regulation rather than a facial sex classification, while reserving broader questions about transgender status and heightened scrutiny. Separate writings are most likely from Thomas/Alito to reject any Bostock-like equal-protection trigger and from Sotomayor (possibly with Jackson) to argue SB1 is sex-referential on its face and fails intermediate scrutiny even accounting for medical uncertainty.
